title: Daily Hydration Guidance
text: General guidance from public health bodies suggests that a typical adult should consume roughly 2 to 3 litres of total water per day, including water from food and other beverages. Requirements vary with body size, physical activity, climate, and health status. Thirst is a reasonable everyday guide for most healthy adults. People with kidney disease, heart failure, or those taking certain medications should follow individualized medical advice rather than general targets. There is no strong evidence that healthy adults benefit from drinking substantially more than their thirst dictates, and very high intakes over short periods can cause dangerous dilution of blood sodium (hyponatremia).
